propertyTaxRate.note: Tax Foundation 'Property Taxes by State' table (Mar 2026): Missouri 0.89% for 2024 (0.91% for 2023), total real taxes paid / total owner-occupied value (ACS B25082, B25090). File value 0.97% is 0.08 pp above, within tolerance.

programs.name: Property Tax Exemption for Total SC Disabled POWs

type.quote: all property, real and personal, of any citizen of this state who is a former prisoner of war ... and who has a total service-connected disability, shall be exempt from taxation

survivingSpouse.quote: Art. X §6 speaks only of the former POW citizen; the STC FAQ does not extend it to a spouse

programs.effectiveChanges: HJR 115 (2026), which would have put a constitutional amendment on the November 2026 ballot extending the homestead exemption to all 100% service-connected veterans and their unremarried surviving spouses, was perfected by the House 4/20/2026 but its last action is 'referred: Select Committee on Property Taxes and the State Tax Commission (S)'; it did not pass the Senate and is not on the 2026 ballot. No change for TY2026 or TY2027.
programs.note: POW-only; the engine must not credit this to a non-POW rated veteran (row has no POW flag, so confirm the engine treats it as non-creditable). Statute citation should be added: Mo. Const. art. X, §6(1).

programs.name: Property Tax Credit for 100% Disabled Veterans

exemptionValue.quote: For all calendar years beginning on or after January 1, 2026 ... credit not to exceed $1,550 in actual property tax or rent equivalent paid up to $1,055, as adjusted for inflation

incomeLimit.quote: For all calendar years beginning on or after January 1, 2026, the maximum upper limit shall be the sum of: (a) Thirty-eight thousand two hundred dollars for claimants with a filing status of single; (b) Forty-two thousand two hundred dollars ... single ... who owned and occupied a homestead for the entire year

incomeLimitMarried.quote: (c) Forty-one thousand dollars ... married filing combined; and (d) Forty-eight thousand dollars ... married filing combined and who owned and occupied a homestead for the entire year

summary.current: MO-PTC: fixed credit up to $1,100 for owner-occupants ($750 renters) at 100% SC — household income ≤ $30,000 single / $34,000 married.
summary.correct: MO-PTC refundable credit. TY2025 claim (filed by April 15, 2026): up to $1,100 owner / $750 renter, income cap $30,000 single / $34,000 married homeowner. TY2026 claim (filed 2027) and later: up to $1,550 owner / $1,055 renter, income cap $42,200 single homeowner ($38,200 renter) / $48,000 married homeowner ($41,000 renter), indexed to CPI from Jan 1, 2027. 100% SC veterans exclude VA payments from household income.
summary.quote: The one hundred percent service-connected disabled veteran shall not be required to list veterans payments and benefits

ratingRequired.quote: the claimant or spouse is a veteran ... who became one hundred percent disabled as a result of such service

programs.effectiveChanges: RSMo 135.030 as amended by H.B. 594 & 508 (2025), effective Aug 28, 2025: for calendar years beginning on or after Jan 1, 2026 the maximum credit rises to $1,550 (owners) / $1,055 (renters) and the income caps to $38,200 / $42,200 (single) and $41,000 / $48,000 (married), with annual CPI indexing from Jan 1, 2027. The 2025 MO-PTC instructions still show $1,100 / $30,000 / $34,000 because they cover the TY2025 claim. HB 1430 (2025), which would have removed the income cap entirely for 100% disabled veterans, died ('Referred: Emerging Issues (H)', no hearing) and its text is not in the current statute.
programs.note: Lead resolved: the HB 1430 income-cap repeal was NOT enacted, but a different 2025 bill (H.B. 594 & 508) raised the caps and the credit for TY2026+. The row should carry both year-sets or switch to the TY2026 figures with a note; the 'excludes most working households' sentence is still true but less so.

summary: The MO-PTC row is stale for TY2026: H.B. 594 & 508 (2025) raised the maximum credit to $1,550 owner / $1,055 renter and the income caps to $42,200 single / $48,000 married homeowners for calendar years from Jan 1, 2026, with CPI indexing from 2027; HB 1430's veteran income-cap repeal died. The POW-only full exemption is unchanged (HJR 115 to extend it to all 100% veterans died in the Senate), and the 0.97% tax rate is within tolerance of the Tax Foundation 2024 figure.
